linguisticJustification: The kanji compound 『選定』 (selection, choice) consists of 選 (せん) and 定 (てい), pronounced 『せんてい』. Option B is the correct phonetic reading.
The kanji compound 『冷静』 (calm, composed) consists of 冷 (れい) and 静 (せい), pronounced 『れいせい』. Option C is the correct phonetic reading.
The kanji compound 『刷新』 (reform, renewal) undergoes sokuon gemination: 刷 (さつ) + 新 (しん) -> 『さっしん』. Option B is the correct phonetic reading.
The kanji compound 『対立』 (opposition, confrontation) consists of 対 (たい) and 立 (りつ), pronounced 『たいりつ』. Option A is the correct phonetic reading.
The kanji compound 『腐食』 (corrosion, etching) consists of 腐 (ふ) and 食 (しょく), pronounced 『ふしょく』. Option D is the correct phonetic reading.
The verb collocation for deliberating/reviewing a business plan is 『事業計画を検討する』 (けんとう = 検討). Option C provides the correct kanji orthography.
The standard collocation for reaching an agreement after negotiation is 『合意に達した』 (たっした = 達した). Option A provides the correct kanji orthography.
The term for social disparity or economic inequality is 『格差』 (かくさ), as in 『社会的な格差の是正』. Option B provides the correct kanji orthography.
The verb for securing or ensuring an emergency power supply is 『確保する』 (かくほ = 確保). Option C provides the correct kanji orthography.
Restoring trust or reputation is written as 『信頼を回復する』 (かいふく = 回復). 快復 is restricted to physical recovery from illness. Option D is the correct kanji orthography.
The standard prefix negating 現実的 (realistic) is 非-, forming 『非現実的』 (unrealistic, surreal). None of the other prefixes (無, 不, 未) attach to 現実的. Option C is correct.
The prefix denoting non-membership attached to 会員 (member) is 非-, forming 『非会員』 (non-member). Option B is correct.
The suffix attached to energy-saving specifications for appliances is -型, forming 『省エネルギー型の家電』 (energy-efficient type/model appliances). Option D is correct.
The compound verb for exceeding or surpassing projected profits is 『予想を上回る』 (うわまわる). Option B provides the correct kanji 上.
The prefix indicating not yet developed attached to 開発 is 未-, forming 『未開発の自然』 (untouched/undeveloped nature). Option C is correct.
The onomatopoeia describing tired, strained, or irritated eyes from prolonged screen exposure is 『目がしょぼしょぼする』. Option B is the exact fit.
The idiomatic collocation for a painful or reluctant managerial decision is 『苦渋の決断』 (a tough, bitter decision). Option C is correct.
The standard adverb collocating with train timetable disruption is 『ダイヤが大幅に乱れている』 (significantly/drastically disrupted). Option B is correct.
Describing an academic paper structure that is thorough, meticulous, and free of logical leaps requires 『構成が綿密』 (meticulous structure). Option B is correct.
The idiom for pulling ahead of or opening a lead over competitors is 『ライバル企業に差をつけた』 (差をつける). Option C is correct.
The adjective describing greeting someone with a pleasant, smiling demeanor to make a good first impression is にこやか (smilingly, cheerfully). Option B is semantically correct.
concerns: Particle nuance: Modern standard Japanese overwhelmingly prefers 『にこやかに挨拶ができる』 with particle に rather than と. While にこやかと is attested in literary/traditional usage, にこやかに is the standard contemporary form.

linguisticJustification: The fixed expression for being trapped/confined inside an elevator during a power failure is 『エレベーターの閉じ込めに遭う』. Option B (閉じ込め) is the correct verbal noun.
The adverb 『ざっと』 means briefly, roughly, or cursorily (e.g. ざっと確認する), which directly matches 『おおまかに』 (Option B).
『皮肉』 refers to sarcasm, cynicism, or snide remarks. The closest synonym is 『嫌味』 (いやみ, Option C).
The onomatopoeic adverb 『ばったり（出会う）』 means bumping into someone by chance or unexpectedly, paraphrased as 『偶然に』 (Option B).
『頓挫（とんざ）』 means a plan or project stalling, collapsing, or suffering a setback midway. This directly equates to 『途中で挫折』 (Option C).
The idiom 『意に介さない』 means paying no mind or not caring about external criticism, which is synonymous with 『気に留めない』 (Option B).
『手薄（てうす）』 specifically denotes being undermanned, short of personnel, or having insufficient security/defenses. Option B (『連休中は警備員が手薄になるため……』) exemplifies the canonical usage.
『配慮（はいりょ）』 means consideration or care for others, taking their circumstances into account (〜に配慮する). Option A (『高齢者や車椅子の利用者に配慮して……』) correctly applies this to accommodating vulnerable station users.
『無難（ぶなん）』 means safe, prudent, and free from the risk of blunder or criticism. Option B (『落ち着いた色のスーツを着ていくのが無難だ』) is the standard idiomatic usage when selecting safe attire.
『目途（めど）』 means prospects, outlook, or target. The set phrase 『目途が立つ』 means prospects/outlook have been established, as in 『資金調達の目途が立ち……』 (Option A).
『妥協（だきょう）』 means compromise or conceding on one's standards. Option A (『どんなに困難な壁にぶつかっても、最後まで決して妥協しない』) represents the canonical usage of refusing to lower one's standards.
The set phrase for finding or carving out time amidst a hectic schedule is 『スケジュールの合間を縫って』 (合間を縫う). Option A is the correct idiomatic verb phrase.
The grammar pattern 〜とあって expresses that because of a special status or situation, a natural result follows: 『プロの料理人とあって、包丁の手入れには人一倍気を使っている』. Option A is correct.
Following the premise 『事態がここまで悪化した以上、もはや……』 (now that things have deteriorated this far), the inevitable consequence is having no choice but to apologize: 『社長自ら謝罪せざるを得ない』 (Option B).
The grammar pattern 〜ならでは（の） denotes something uniquely possible for or characteristic of a master or special entity: 『熟練の職人ならではの技だ』 (a skill unique to veteran artisans). Option B is correct.

The suffix 〜がたい attaches to the masu-stem of cognitive verbs to express that something is practically impossible or exceedingly difficult to do emotionally/intellectually: 『一般の人には理解しがたいものだった』. Option C is correct.

The grammar construction 『どんなに〜ようと（も）』 expresses an extreme concessive condition ('no matter how much...'). Paired with どんなに, 『進歩しようと』 (Option A) forms the standard N2 structure 『どんなに科学技術が進歩しようと、……できない』.
concerns: Distractor overlap: 『〜したところで』 (even if... it is futile) can colloquially express a similar concessive nuance, though 『どんなに……ようと』 is the canonical textbook pairing.
